newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium slides to lowest in a month.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium slides to lowest in a month.

text.p: LME aluminium slipped to the softest levels in a month on Tuesday afternoon, dragging other base metals with it, as a correction extended lower.
Copper headed towards the $2,200 mark, lead extended Monday's losses and notched up fresh 15-1/2 month lows, but zinc was resilient.
"Many of the metals seem to be in a correction phase after having seen some very good run-ups," said analyst Martin Squires at Rudolf Wolff.
Fund selling fed weakness in aluminium after prices on Monday broke out of a $1,600-$1,650 range seen for weeks.
Prices touched a low of $1,534, the weakest since January 2, but bounced to end the kerb at $1,547, a $38 loss.
Support should be seen at $1,533, the January 2 low, at $1,510, the 200-day moving average, and at the $1,500 psychological mark, Squires said.

Players would likely test lower levels in the coming days but aluminium's long term uptrend would not be in danger unless prices fell below $1,500. "I think we are seeing some good buying opportunities," he said.
Copper also eased, but a less-than-expected stocks build of 2,650 tonnes and the backwardation helped prop up the market.
Three month prices ended at their low of $2,212, down $19 on the day and forming a bearish outside day. A test of the $2,200 level was likely in the near term, analysts said.
But an ascending triangle still seemed to be forming on the charts, with the break-out point at $2,281, indicating a move to $2,450, Squires said.
Support was pegged at $2,140 and $2,077, he added.
Spreads were narrower, with the cash/threes indicated around a $150 backwardation compared with about $180 on Monday.
But nearby spreads were still strong, with cash for a day earlier trading at $22.50, near the LME limit.
Lead etched out a fresh 15-1/2 month low of $634, equalling the nadir on October 18, 1995.
But it rebounded slightly to finish the kerb at $644, a loss of $13 from Monday.

The physical market has been slow recently, with the US battery replacement market weaker than expected, traders and industry sources said. Italy is a soft spot in Europe as ceramic and auto sectors see sluggish sales, they added.
Nickel settled at its low of $7,730, down $105 on the day and off recent highs near $8,000. But Tuesday's low was above Monday's weakest level of $7,690.
A correction had been expected, since the market's blistering rise had pushed it into overbought territory and it needed to let off some steam, analysts said.
Zinc and tin bucked the trend, ignoring the weakness in the other metals to end $1 higher at $1,176 and unchanged at $5,920, respectively.
Alloy was softer at $1,460 versus $1,495/500.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
